name: Mulle
description: Mulle (also known as Swedish Casino or Nordic Casino) is a fishing card game popular in Sweden and Finland. It is a variant of the international Casino game family, where players capture cards from a central layout by matching values. The game features unique Nordic scoring rules and special values for certain cards.

overview.description: Mulle (also known as Swedish Casino or Nordic Casino) is a fishing card game popular in Sweden and Finland. It is a variant of the international Casino game family, where players capture cards from a central layout by matching values. The game features unique Nordic scoring rules and special values for certain cards.

history.origins: Mulle is part of the Casino game family that spread throughout the world. The Nordic variant developed specific rules for scoring and card values, distinguishing it from other national variants.
timeline: Traditional: Developed in Sweden and Finland
20th Century: Rules formalized in Nordic game collections
Present: Played in Scandinavia and by Nordic communities abroad
history.cultural: A popular family game in Sweden and Finland, often played in homes and summer cottages. The game is part of the Nordic card game tradition.
history.evolution: The game maintains the core Casino mechanic of capturing by matching, with Nordic variations in card values and scoring.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Cards have numerical capture values: 2-10 = face value, Jack = 11, Queen = 12, King = 13, Ace = 1 or 14 (player's choice).
setup.dealing: 4 cards to each player and 4 cards face-up to the table. Remaining cards form the stock.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the table by matching their values. Score points for specific captured cards and achievements.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns playing one card from hand. A card can capture table cards of the same value, or combinations of table cards that sum to the played card's value. If no capture is possible, the card is added to the table.
keyRules: Can capture combinations that sum to played card
Score for specific cards and achievements

strategy.basic: Try to capture high-value cards (10 of Diamonds, 2 of Spades, Aces). Clear the table when possible for sweep bonuses. Remember which cards have been played.
strategy.intermediate: Use building to set up captures for your strong cards. Force opponents to leave valuable cards on the table. Track the distribution of spades.
strategy.advanced: Card counting is essential. Calculate probabilities of opponents holding specific cards. Use building and blocking to control the table. Time your sweeps for maximum advantage.
tips: The 10 of Diamonds is usually the most valuable single card
Clearing the table (sweep) gives a bonus point
Track which spades have been played - most spades scores points
Building can set up multiple captures but risks opponents stealing
Aces are valuable both as captures and for scoring

scoring.description: Points awarded for: most cards, most spades, 10 of Diamonds, 2 of Spades, and Aces. Exact values vary by regional rules.
scoring.winCondition: First to reach target score (typically 16 or 21 points) or highest score when stock is exhausted.
